solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rubbish song covered repeatedly by one like Kylie

indicators.note: the song and rubbish are wrapped on both sides by the two copies of 'one'
'one' is used twice, once on each side

parts.note: AN is the indefinite article, meaning one
a tip is a rubbish dump
an ode is a lyric poem or song

explanation.surface: A trashy pop number sung over and over by an Australian star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by one' looks like it names the singer, but 'one' is wordplay used twice, once at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: Kylie Minogue is Australian, and Antipodean describes someone from Australia or New Zealand.

clue.text: Child in casualty hurt

indicators.note: the child abbreviation is placed inside the hospital department letters

parts.note: A and E (Accident and Emergency) is the British hospital casualty department

explanation.surface: A youngster in the emergency department is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurt, as a verb, is to throb with pain, a synonym.

clue.text: PC displays this part of medal after duty

parts.note: a task is a duty or job
a bar is the strip on a medal ribbon, added for a further award

explanation.surface: A police constable shows off a bit of his decoration after a spell on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like police constable, but here it is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer screen shows the strip of program buttons along its bottom edge, so the definition describes it.

clue.text: Dispassionate Greek character, later seen again in local, so drunk

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the repeated Greek letter is placed inside the scrambled pub-and-so letters
drunk letters are scrambled, so this signals an anagram

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the same Greek letter turns up a second time, among the mixed letters

explanation.surface: A calm Greek, spotted again later in the pub, is now tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' gives LOSOCAL from the clue's local and so; 'local' is British slang for a nearby pub, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Being philosophical about a setback means taking it calmly and dispassionately.

clue.text: Heading for dentist, Reginald heard instrument excavating canal?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so this takes the start of dentist
heard says the short name must be spoken and spelt by its sound

parts.note: Reg is the short form of Reginald

explanation.surface: A dentist's tool heard drilling a root canal.
explanation.walkthrough: Canal suggests a root canal at the dentist, but it is a waterway being cleared of mud.
explanation.definitionFit: The device scoops silt from the bed of a river or canal, so it excavates one.

clue.text: Remove member from team, up at ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed or reduced to bits, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Dropping a player from a side, at the stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A member here is a limb; cutting one off is the surgical sense.

clue.text: Wound was bleeding, initially needing this?

definitions.text: Wound was bleeding, initially needing this?

indicators.note: wound read as twisted (rhymes with sound) signals the letters are rearranged
initially takes the opening letter of bleeding

explanation.surface: A bleeding cut might call for cotton wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury but signals the anagram of WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad of absorbent material is used to clean or mop up a bleeding cut.

clue.text: Legal expert upheld properties of soap?

indicators.note: in a down clue, held up means the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: a doctor of law (DR OF LAW) is a legal expert

explanation.surface: A lawyer backed the case about a soap firm's assets.
explanation.walkthrough: Soap is a TV soap opera: this is the fictional London borough where EastEnders, a long-running BBC soap, is set.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional borough holds the houses and businesses of the TV soap, all its properties.

clue.text: Miss gets overawed by more evil TV series

indicators.note: split as over-awed: the miss word sits under the comparative, which goes over it

parts.note: badder is a colloquial comparative of bad
to lack is to miss or be without

explanation.surface: A young woman is intimidated by a nastier rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackadder is a British TV comedy series starring Rowan Atkinson.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom ran on the BBC in four series, an example of a TV series.

clue.text: Militant fired reactionary having socks on the outside

indicators.note: the hosiery word sits round the other part

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks

indicators.note: reactionary means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: lit means set alight, fired

explanation.surface: A sacked right-wing activist wearing socks over everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Militant and hostile both describe an aggressive, combative attitude.

clue.text: Secretary and clerk discussed some of 23

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: discussed means talked of, so the clerk word is taken by sound

parts.note: a teller is a bank clerk

explanation.surface: An office secretary and a clerk talked through part of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is KNEE, the answer to 23 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The kneecap is a bone forming part of the knee joint.

clue.text: A Tudor manor matches building contractor's extreme character

indicators.note: building puts the letters together in a new form
the extreme letter is the final one of contractor's

explanation.surface: A Tudor manor house is a fit for the builder's grand personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Tudor' is a figure from the Tudor period: he was Archbishop of Canterbury under Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: The archbishop lived and died in the Tudor era, burnt under Mary I, so he is one Tudor figure.

clue.text: Punished hoodlum, in empty backstreet ransacking boot, with fine

indicators.note: the hoodlum sits inside the emptied backstreet
an empty word has lost its middle, keeping only its ends

parts.note: a rough is a hooligan or thug

indicators.note: ransacking throws things about, so the letters of boot are jumbled

parts.note: OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: A thug in a deserted alley rifling a car boot is punished and fined.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being made to answer for wrongdoing means punished.

clue.text: Pet Rescue arranged to collect money, to feed protected animal

indicators.note: the inner letters feed into the animal word, going inside it

parts.note: bats are a protected species in Britain

indicators.note: the jumbled letters gather the money abbreviation inside them
arranged means set in a new order, an anagram

explanation.surface: An animal charity organised a fundraiser to feed a protected creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed from Burma is a domestic cat, kept as a pet.

clue.text: Eradicate overly posh accent (upper-class rearing)

indicators.note: rearing up, like a horse, turns the whole string back to front

parts.note: too means overly or excessively
RP is received pronunciation, the standard posh English accent

explanation.surface: Stamp out an overdone plummy accent from an upper-class upbringing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull out by the roots is to eradicate, root being the source of that word.

clue.text: Left afar, ultimately amidst environment that's beach-like?

definitions.text: Left afar, ultimately amidst environment that's beach-like?

indicators.note: the end letters go in the middle of the sandy word

parts.note: sanded means covered with sand, as a beach is

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Cast away far off, ending up somewhere sandy like a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: As an all-in-one, the whole clue paints a castaway left on a sandy shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A person left behind and unable to get away is marooned, as on a beach.

clue.text: American obtains celebrity through training egotistic new kids on the block

definitions.text: egotistic new kids on the block

indicators.note: the American abbreviation obtains, taking in, the rest
the celebrity goes through the middle of the training letters

parts.note: PT is physical training
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A US star found fame through training a boy band.
explanation.walkthrough: New Kids on the Block was an American boy band; here it just means newcomers.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-important newcomers who rise fast are pushy arrivistes, or new kids on the block.

clue.text: Woman, alongside husband by mirror, rejected confectionery?

parts.note: Miss is a title for an unmarried woman
to ape is to mirror or copy

explanation.surface: A woman with her husband by the looking glass turns down sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, misshapes are sweets or biscuits sold cheap for being imperfectly formed.
explanation.definitionFit: Factory rejects that came out the wrong form are sold off as such, so they are rejected confectionery.

clue.text: Drink and sex perhaps priorities for Richard Burton and Elizabeth Taylor

parts.note: she stands for the female sex

indicators.note: priorities are things put first, so take the first letters of the four names

explanation.surface: Drinking and sex were said to top the couple's list of priorities.
explanation.walkthrough: Burton and Taylor were famously married film stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fruit drink is called by this name, especially in older and Middle Eastern usage.

clue.text: Disorder in sheep, as one's missing graze

indicators.note: one is missing, so the numeral for one leaves the word

parts.note: scrapie is a brain disease of sheep
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sheep ailment, as one animal has gone missing from the grazing.
explanation.walkthrough: Graze looks like what sheep do but is the noun for a skin abrasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A graze is a light wound where skin is rubbed off, a synonym.

clue.text: Terrible samba dancing curbed close to halfway line

indicators.note: the samba letters hem in, curb, the letter from halfway
dancing letters move about, so samba is rearranged
close is the end, so take the final letter of halfway

explanation.surface: Awful samba moves, stopped near the halfway line of a football pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysmal means appallingly bad, a close synonym of the definition.

clue.text: The one setting levy on a spirit abroad

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
a tax is a levy

explanation.surface: The person imposing a duty on a foreign liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: This Greek brandy is a spirit drunk abroad, in Greece.

clue.text: Injured PE teacher, around hospital, stops to look for special treatment

indicators.note: the mixed letters stop, plug, the middle of the look word

parts.note: to spy is to look or watch
PE, physical education, is taken as written

indicators.note: the jumbled teacher letters go around the hospital abbreviation
injured means damaged, so the letters of teacher are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hurt PE teacher, round at the hospital, stops off to seek special care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' rearranges teacher into ECTHERA; PE stays in order at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy for speech problems is a specialist treatment for children and stroke patients.

clue.text: Eager to shift latest joint

indicators.note: the latest, last, letter of the eager word is shifted to another place

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: Keen to move the most recent cannabis cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint looks like slang for a cannabis cigarette but is the body joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg's hinge between thigh and shin is one joint of the body.

clue.text: Pie last seen at his workplace?

definitions.meaning: a fruit pie with a scone-like topping
a last is the foot-shaped form a shoemaker works on

explanation.surface: A pie last spotted where he works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like 'most recently', but it is the shoemaker's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe mender works at a last, and the same word names a baked fruit pudding.

clue.text: Once a pauper, active coxswain ditched hard drug

indicators.note: ditched means thrown out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a helmsman steers a boat, as a coxswain does
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
E is short for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A former down-and-out who once steered a boat has given up hard drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word meant someone living on charity, a historic pauper.

clue.text: Rag-and-bone man's centre parting?

parts.note: tat is cheap junk, the stuff a rag-and-bone dealer collects

indicators.note: the centre is the middle letter of man's word

explanation.surface: A junk collector's hair parting down the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag-and-bone man is a British street dealer in old junk; 'parting' looks like hair but means a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal goodbye is said at a parting.

clue.text: Outside in elements, chaplain defends wrong footwear

indicators.note: the outside letters of elements are its first and last
the chaplain word guards the wrong word by surrounding it

parts.note: padre is a forces chaplain
ill as an adverb means wrongly, badly

explanation.surface: Out in the weather, a chaplain stands up for improper shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: These rope-soled canvas shoes are a kind of footwear.
